title: Managing a Prima Donna
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article profiles the workplace Prima Donna, a talented but difficult colleague whose inflated sense of self-worth makes them resistant to feedback and hard to manage. It traces how these dynamics usually form: a prior leader avoids the conflict of confronting the person's ego and instead placates them to keep the peace, which only entrenches the behavior further. The piece is especially interested in what happens when a new leader inherits a Prima Donna, since that leader has no history of coddling them and typically triggers friction by evaluating them objectively for the first time. It concludes that consistent, candid feedback, applied without exception, is what ultimately dissolves the Prima Donna dynamic.
points: A Prima Donna is a talented colleague with an inflated, oversized view of their own contribution.
Prima Donnas are especially resistant to feedback and criticism about their performance.
Prior leaders often placate Prima Donnas to avoid conflict, which reinforces the behavior.
New leaders who evaluate a Prima Donna objectively for the first time often trigger real friction.
Consistent, candid feedback without exception is what breaks the Prima Donna pattern.
quotes: Some colleagues think so highly of themselves that it's a wonder their feet stay on the ground.
Prima Donna is a derogatory term that originates from the Italian Opera.
Because they believe they are the star of the show and invaluable, Prima Donnas don't take feedback well.
It is better to tolerate the Prima Donna than to suffer through their bad-tempered reactions to criticism or to lose them.
Prima Donnas become who they are precisely because others fear the backlash of telling them the truth.
Good leaders don't protect anyone from feedback and constructive criticism.
